newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rights body to consider final report.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rights body to consider final report.

text.p: Indonesia's official National Comission on Human Rights will consider its final report on Jakarta's July 27 riots at a meeting on Tuesday but is not expected to release its findings immediately, a senior member said.
Deputy Chairman Marzuki Darusman said it was also expected to elect a new chairman after the death in June of its founding head, former Supreme Court chief justice Ali Said.
"We will be discussing the report in a plenary session but we may need a few days to finalise it," Darusman told Reuters.
The commission's preliminary report on August 31 found at least five people died and 149 were injured in the riots and 74 people had been reported missing.

The human rights body, founded in 1993, came under pressure from the government and the military to justify its preliminary findings as the military had said only four people had died and had not acknowledged any people were missing.
